Rating Distribution

71.9% of reviews are 5 stars, with an overall average of 4.41 out of 5. Only 9.9% are negative (1-2 stars). The dataset skews heavily positive - most Home Depot customers are satisfied with their purchases.

Sentiment Analysis - VADER vs Star Rating

I ran VADER and TextBlob sentiment analysis on all review text. VADER correlates 0.681 with star ratings - what people write generally matches what they rate. TextBlob was weaker at 0.532, likely because VADER is better tuned for product review language.

Sentiment-Rating Alignment

96.1% of reviews have text sentiment that matches their star rating. But 3.9% show mismatches - 192 reviews had positive language with low stars, and 91 had negative language with high stars. Some customers write balanced feedback even when dissatisfied.

Word Frequency - Positive vs Negative

The language gap is clear. Positive reviews focus on appearance and ease - easy, beautiful, perfect, sturdy. Negative reviews focus on failure and disappointment - disappointed, return, broken, cheap. This tells us customers value aesthetics and simplicity above all.

Complaint Themes

Quality and durability is the number one complaint, appearing in 41% of all negative reviews. Customer service issues (31%), difficult assembly (30%), shipping problems (27%), and products not matching descriptions (27%) follow. These are actionable categories a business can target.

Praise Themes

Appearance and design leads at 53% of positive reviews - customers care deeply about how products look. Recommendation (49%), durability (41%), easy setup (40%), and perfect fit (37%) round out the top praise themes. Interestingly, value for money only appears in 8% of positive reviews.

Category Satisfaction

Lighting has the highest satisfaction at 4.62 avg rating with just 1.5% one-star reviews. Appliances rank lowest at 4.00 with a 14% one-star rate. Outdoors is the largest category (4,761 reviews) sitting at a strong 4.54.

Price vs Satisfaction

Price has almost no correlation with satisfaction (r = -0.015). Expensive products are not rated meaningfully higher or lower than cheap ones. The $25-50 range actually has the highest average rating at 4.48. This suggests product quality matters more than price point.

Review Length by Rating

4-star reviews are the longest at 62 words average, while 1-star reviews are the shortest at 38 words. This was unexpected - I assumed unhappy customers would write the most. It seems moderate satisfaction drives the most detailed feedback.

Manufacturer Satisfaction

GE leads at 4.70 avg rating (20 reviews). Alpine Corporation dominates volume with 5,855 reviews at 4.51. On the other end, Home Decorators Collection (27% negative) and iFit (43% negative) have the worst satisfaction rates among manufacturers with enough data.
